rationale: The workflow is a Rust CI pipeline with no dependency cache. Every job that compiles code (clippy, test, test-msvr, autobahn) re-downloads crates from the cargo registry on each run. The P-LIT-GHA-CACHE pattern (Cache dependency downloads) is supported by observational evidence from the ICSE 2024 GitHub Actions workflows study, which reports modest aggregate VM-time savings from caching dependency downloads. Preconditions are met: repeated dependency fetching occurs on every run, and Cargo.toml (confirmed present in the repository) can serve as a cache-key input. The change adds actions/cache@v4 for ~/.cargo/registry and ~/.cargo/git before cargo commands in the jobs that compile, using Cargo.toml as the cache key with a restore-key fallback. No build or test steps are removed, no permissions are weakened, no secrets or deployment operations are added, and no new network access beyond the existing GitHub Actions cache service is introduced. The fmt job is excluded because cargo fmt does not compile or download dependencies, so caching would add overhead without benefit.
